content.title: Nuggets vs. Suns: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/24/26)
content.text: The Denver Nuggets (44–28) face the Phoenix Suns (40–32) tonight at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix. Denver enters the matchup on a two-game winning streak and sits fourth in the Western Conference standings, with just half a game separating the Nuggets from the sixth-place Houston Rockets. On Sunday, the Nuggets defeated the Portland Trail Blazers 128–112 behind another standout performance from Nikola Jokic. The reigning MVP recorded his 28th triple-double of an injury-interrupted season, finishing with 22 points, 14 rebounds, and 14 assists. Jamal Murray also scored 22 points, with the duo combining to hit six three-pointers. Peyton Watson returned to the lineup in that game, scoring 14 points in 20 minutes off the bench in his first appearance in more than a month. He will sit out tonight’s contest, the front end of a back-to-back. Denver jumped out to a fast start, leading 42–40 after the first quarter and never trailing the rest of the way. The Nuggets built a lead as large as 20 points while shooting 54% from the field and 39% from beyond the arc. The Suns, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a decisive 120–98 victory over the Toronto Raptors on Sunday. Devin Booker led the way with 25 points on 9-of-15 shooting, while Jalen Green added 20. Collin Gillespie contributed 16 points on an efficient 6-of-9 performance, knocking down four three-pointers. Phoenix shot 52% from the field and an impressive 45% from deep. Despite the win, the recent skid has left the Suns 3.5 games behind the Rockets for the sixth and final automatic playoff spot. Phoenix is currently positioned in the top play-in tournament berth as the regular season enters its final stretch. Denver has the edge, given the seemingly limitless ceiling for the Jokic-Murray tandem. But Phoenix can take this one if it gets big nights from both Booker and Green, and efficient scoring from Gillespie. Final Score Prediction: Denver Nuggets 118, Phoenix Suns 114 Injury Report Denver Nuggets Peyton Watson — Out (Hamstring) Phoenix Suns Mark Williams — Out (Foot) Dillon Brooks — Out (Hand) Haywood Highsmith — GTD (Knee) Jordan Goodwin — GTD (Calf) Grayson Allen — GTD (Knee) How to Watch Nuggets vs. Suns Tip-off for tonight’s Nuggets-Suns game is set for 11:00 PM Eastern / 9:00 PM Mountain at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix.
